absolute_risk.quote: The reported incidence of malformation in the offspring of mothers exposed to mycophenolate during pregnancy is 23 to 27% compared with 4 to 5% in transplant patients treated with other immunosuppressants, and 2 to 3% in the overall population.
absolute_risk.source_label: European Medicines Agency press release, 'EMA recommends additional measures to prevent use of mycophenolate in pregnancy'

before_after.text: Women who can become pregnant must use at least one reliable contraceptive method before starting mycophenolate, during treatment and for six weeks after stopping, unless they choose abstinence.
before_after.quote: women of childbearing potential must use at least one form of reliable contraception (see section 4.3) before starting the therapy, during therapy, and for six weeks after stopping the therapy, unless abstinence is the chosen method of contraception.
before_after.source_label: EMA product information, CellCept (mycophenolate mofetil), SmPC section 4.6 Fertility, pregnancy and lactation (EN product information last updated 07/05/2026)

paternal.text: As a precaution, a sexually active man taking mycophenolate or his female partner is recommended to use reliable contraception during his treatment and for at least 90 days after he stops.
paternal.quote: Therefore, the following precautionary measures are recommended: sexually active male patients or their female partners are recommended to use reliable contraception during treatment of the male patient and for at least 90 days after cessation of mycophenolate mofetil.
paternal.source_label: EMA product information, CellCept (mycophenolate mofetil), SmPC section 4.6, subsection Men (EN product information last updated 07/05/2026)

other_effects.text: Beyond malformations, spontaneous abortion has been reported in 45 to 49% of pregnant women exposed to mycophenolate mofetil, against 12 to 33% in solid organ transplant patients on other immunosuppressants.
other_effects.quote: Spontaneous abortions have been reported in 45 to 49% of pregnant women exposed to mycophenolate mofetil, compared to a reported rate of between 12 and 33% in solid organ transplant patients treated with immunosuppressants other than mycophenolate mofetil.
other_effects.source_label: EMA product information, CellCept (mycophenolate mofetil), SmPC section 4.6, subsection Pregnancy (EN product information last updated 07/05/2026)

regulatory.text: The EU product information contraindicates mycophenolate in pregnancy unless there is no suitable alternative treatment to prevent transplant rejection.
regulatory.quote: Therefore, treatment is contraindicated in pregnancy unless there are no suitable alternative treatments to prevent transplant rejection.
regulatory.source_label: EMA product information, CellCept (mycophenolate mofetil), SmPC section 4.4, subsection Teratogenic effects (EN product information last updated 07/05/2026)

monitoring.text: If pregnancy occurs or is suspected during or shortly after treatment, the patient should not stop taking mycophenolate but must contact their doctor immediately.
monitoring.quote: Advice on action if a pregnancy occurs or is suspected during or shortly after being treated with mycophenolate mofetil. Patients will be informed that they should not stop taking mycophenolate mofetil but must contact their doctor immediately.
monitoring.source_label: EMA product information, CellCept (mycophenolate mofetil), Annex II.D, key elements of the educational materials (EN product information last updated 07/05/2026)

evidence_base.text: A US transplant registry cohort covered 382 pregnancies in kidney recipients managed on mycophenolate, grouped by when each woman stopped it, some before conception, so not all were exposed in pregnancy.
evidence_base.quote: Data from the National Transplantation Pregnancy Registry included 382 cases in which KTRs managed on MPA became pregnant. Overall, 22 variables, including the time in which a KTR discontinued MPA, were assessed
evidence_base.source_label: King RW et al., Pregnancy Outcomes Related to Mycophenolate Exposure in Female Kidney Transplant Recipients, Am J Transplant 2017;17(1):151-160, abstract (retrospective cohort, US National Transplantation Pregnancy Registry)

dose.text: In a monkey study, limb defects appeared in the offspring at every dose tested; this is an animal finding and gives no human dose threshold.
dose.quote: Limb abnormalities were seen in the offspring of monkeys that were dosed with lenalidomide during organogenesis. This effect was seen at all doses tested.
dose.source_label: US FDA label, Revlimid (Celgene), section 4.1 Contraindications (Pregnancy), read via openFDA version 41 (DailyMed version 41 published 2026-08-06)

effects.text: In a monkey study, lenalidomide caused limb defects similar to thalidomide's birth defects in humans, and the US label warns it may cause birth defects or embryo-fetal death.
effects.quote: Lenalidomide, a thalidomide analogue, caused limb abnormalities in a developmental monkey study similar to birth defects caused by thalidomide in humans. If lenalidomide is used during pregnancy, it may cause birth defects or embryo-fetal death.
effects.source_label: US FDA label, Revlimid (Celgene), Boxed Warning, Highlights version (Embryo-fetal toxicity)

before_after.text: A woman who can become pregnant must use effective contraception from at least 4 weeks before lenalidomide to at least 4 weeks after, even during interruptions, unless committed to absolute, continuous, monthly-confirmed abstinence.
before_after.quote: for at least 4 weeks before therapy, during therapy, and until at least 4 weeks after lenalidomide therapy and even in case of dose interruption unless the patient commits to absolute and continuous abstinence confirmed on a monthly basis
before_after.source_label: EMA product information, Revlimid (lenalidomide), SmPC section 4.4, Contraception (women of childbearing potential) (EN product information last updated 09/09/2025)

paternal.text: Under the EU product information, men on lenalidomide should use condoms during treatment and dose interruptions and for 1 week after stopping if their partner is pregnant, or could become pregnant without contraception.
paternal.quote: all male patients taking lenalidomide should use condoms throughout treatment duration, during dose interruption and for 1 week after cessation of treatment if their partner is pregnant or of childbearing potential and has no contraception.
paternal.source_label: EMA product information, Revlimid (lenalidomide), SmPC section 4.6, Women of childbearing potential/Contraception in males and females (EN product information last updated 09/09/2025)

other_effects.text: In animal studies, lenalidomide caused embryo death in pregnant rabbits at 20 times the maximum recommended human dose; this is an animal result.
other_effects.quote: Similar studies in pregnant rabbits and rats at 20 times and 200 times the MRHD respectively, produced embryo lethality in rabbits
other_effects.source_label: US FDA label, Revlimid (Celgene), section 8.1 Pregnancy, Animal data, read via openFDA (version 41, effective 2023-03-24)

regulatory.text: The EU product information requires lenalidomide to be prescribed under a Pregnancy Prevention Programme unless there is reliable evidence that the patient does not have childbearing potential.
regulatory.quote: Due to the teratogenic potential, lenalidomide must be prescribed under a Pregnancy Prevention Programme (see section 4.4) unless there is reliable evidence that the patient does not have childbearing potential.
regulatory.source_label: EMA product information, Revlimid (lenalidomide), SmPC section 4.6 (EN product information last updated 09/09/2025)

monitoring.text: If a woman becomes pregnant on lenalidomide, treatment must be stopped and she should be referred to a physician specialised or experienced in teratology for evaluation and advice.
monitoring.quote: If pregnancy occurs in a woman treated with lenalidomide, treatment must be stopped and the patient should be referred to a physician specialised or experienced in teratology for evaluation and advice.
monitoring.source_label: EMA product information, Revlimid (lenalidomide), SmPC section 4.6 (EN product information last updated 09/09/2025)

evidence_base.text: The US label bases its pregnancy warning on lenalidomide's mechanism of action and on animal studies; the label's pregnancy data section presents animal data only.
evidence_base.quote: Based on the mechanism of action [see Clinical Pharmacology (12.1) ] and findings from animal studies [see Data] , REVLIMID can cause embryo-fetal harm when administered to a pregnant female
evidence_base.source_label: US FDA label, Revlimid (Celgene), section 8.1 Pregnancy, Risk Summary, read via openFDA (version 41, effective 2023-03-24)

window.text: The EMA assessment places the sensitive period at 21 to 35 days after conception, counted from conception rather than from the last period, when the limbs and major organs form.
window.quote: This sensitive period is 21-35 days after conception, a crucial time for the development of the limbs and major organ systems
window.source_label: EMA CHMP assessment report, Thalidomide Pharmion (now Thalidomide BMS), non-clinical section on embryo-foetal development

dose.text: The current US label says that even a single capsule, of any strength, taken during pregnancy can cause severe birth defects.
dose.quote: Even a single dose [1 capsule (regardless of strength)] taken by a pregnant woman during her pregnancy can cause severe birth defects.
dose.source_label: US FDA label, THALOMID (Celgene), boxed warning, via openFDA (DailyMed SPL v25)

effects.text: Birth defects named in the EU product information include missing or partly missing arms and/or legs (amelia, phocomelia, hemimelia), small ears with blind or absent ear canals, eye defects, heart disease and kidney abnormalities.
effects.quote: ectromelia (amelia, phocomelia, hemimelia) of the upper and/or lower extremities, microtia with abnormality of the external acoustic meatus (blind or absent), middle and internal ear lesions (less frequent), ocular lesions (anophthalmia, microphthalmia), congenital heart disease, renal abnormalities.
effects.source_label: EMA SmPC, Thalidomide BMS 50 mg hard capsules, section 4.6

absolute_risk.text: The EU product information says thalidomide causes severe birth defects at a high frequency, about 30%, and gives no comparison rate.
absolute_risk.quote: Thalidomide is a powerful human teratogen, inducing a high frequency (about 30 %) of severe and live-threatening birth defects
absolute_risk.source_label: EMA SmPC, Thalidomide BMS 50 mg hard capsules, section 4.6

before_after.text: EU labelling requires women of childbearing potential to use one effective contraceptive from at least 4 weeks before to at least 4 weeks after treatment, interruptions included, unless committed to absolute, continuous, monthly-confirmed abstinence.
before_after.quote: method of contraception for at least 4 weeks before start of treatment, during treatment, and until at least 4 weeks after thalidomide treatment and even in case of dose interruption unless the patient commits to absolute and continuous abstinence
before_after.source_label: EMA SmPC, Thalidomide BMS 50 mg hard capsules, section 4.4 (Pregnancy Prevention Programme, Contraception)

paternal.text: As a precaution, EU labelling requires men to use condoms during treatment, dose interruptions and for at least 7 days after stopping if their partner is pregnant, or could become pregnant without effective contraception.
paternal.quote: as a precaution all male patients must use condoms during treatment, during dose interruption and for at least 7 days following discontinuation of treatment if their partner is pregnant or is of childbearing potential not using effective contraception.
paternal.source_label: EMA SmPC, Thalidomide BMS 50 mg hard capsules, section 4.4 (Men)

other_effects.text: The US label reports death at or shortly after birth in about 40% of infants, without saying which infants were counted.
other_effects.quote: Mortality at or shortly after birth has been reported in about 40% of infants.
other_effects.source_label: US FDA label, THALOMID (Celgene), section 5.1 Embryo-Fetal Toxicity, via openFDA (SPL version 25)

regulatory.text: The EU label contraindicates thalidomide in pregnancy, and in women who could become pregnant unless every condition of its Pregnancy Prevention Programme is met.
regulatory.quote: Thalidomide is contraindicated during pregnancy and in women of childbearing potential unless all the conditions of the Pregnancy Prevention Programme are met
regulatory.source_label: EMA SmPC, Thalidomide BMS 50 mg hard capsules, section 4.6 (see also section 4.3)

monitoring.text: If pregnancy occurs, the EU label says thalidomide must be stopped immediately and the patient should be referred to a physician specialised or experienced in teratology for evaluation and advice.
monitoring.quote: If pregnancy occurs in a woman treated with thalidomide, treatment must be stopped immediately and the patient should be referred to a physician specialised or experienced in teratology for evaluation and advice.
monitoring.source_label: EMA SmPC, Thalidomide BMS 50 mg hard capsules, section 4.6

evidence_base.text: The US label gives no count of exposed pregnancies and names oral ingestion as the only maternal exposure known to cause birth defects, with no specific data on risks of skin absorption or inhalation.
evidence_base.quote: Oral ingestion is the only type of maternal THALOMID exposure known to result in drug-associated birth defects. There are no specific data available regarding the reproductive risks of cutaneous absorption or inhalation of THALOMID
evidence_base.source_label: US FDA label, THALOMID (Celgene), section 5.1 Embryo-Fetal Toxicity, via openFDA (SPL version 25)

window.text: The US label names no gestational week and says that potentially any fetus exposed during pregnancy can be affected.
window.quote: Potentially any fetus exposed during pregnancy can be affected. There are no accurate means of determining prenatally whether an exposed fetus has been affected.
window.source_label: US FDA label, ABSORICA / ABSORICA LD (Sun Pharmaceutical), boxed warning and section 5.1, via openFDA (DailyMed SPL v21)

dose.text: The US label says the risk of life-threatening birth defects is extremely high if pregnancy occurs while taking any amount, even for short periods.
dose.quote: There is an extremely high risk that life-threatening birth defects will result if pregnancy occurs while taking any amount of ABSORICA/ABSORICA LD even for short periods of time.
dose.source_label: US FDA label, ABSORICA / ABSORICA LD (Sun Pharmaceutical), section 5.1, via openFDA (DailyMed SPL v21)

effects.text: The US label lists malformations of the face, eyes, ears, skull, central nervous system, heart and blood vessels, and thymus and parathyroid glands, but not limb defects.
effects.quote: Major congenital malformations that have been documented following isotretinoin exposure include malformations of the face, eyes, ears, skull, central nervous system, cardiovascular system, and thymus and parathyroid glands.
effects.source_label: US FDA label, ABSORICA / ABSORICA LD (Sun Pharmaceutical), section 8.1 human data, via openFDA (DailyMed SPL v21)

absolute_risk.text: The EMA's safety committee says human data show a risk of retinoid embryopathy in up to 30% of exposed fetuses, for oral retinoids as a group, without a comparison rate.
absolute_risk.quote: The human data on congenital malformations after oral retinoid exposure shows a significant risk of retinoid embryopathy (of up to 30% of fetuses exposed)
absolute_risk.source_label: EMA PRAC assessment report, Article 31 referral on retinoid-containing medicinal products, section 3 benefit-risk balance

before_after.text: The French label requires contraception from at least 1 month before isotretinoin, throughout treatment and for at least 1 month after stopping, even in women without periods.
before_after.quote: Une méthode de contraception doit être utilisée pendant au moins 1 mois avant le début du traitement, pendant toute la durée du traitement et pendant au moins 1 mois après l'arrêt du traitement par l’isotrétinoïne, même en cas d’aménorrhée.
before_after.source_label: ANSM, RCP ISOTRETINOINE ACNETRAIT 20 mg, capsule molle, section 4.4 (Programme de Prévention de la Grossesse, Contraception), RCP updated 30/07/2026

paternal.text: The French label says available data suggest that maternal exposure through the semen of men taking isotretinoin is too low to be linked to the drug's teratogenic effects.
paternal.quote: Les données disponibles suggèrent que le niveau d'exposition maternelle à partir du sperme des patients traités par ISOTRETINOINE ACNETRAIT 20 mg, capsule molle n’est pas suffisant pour être associé aux effets tératogènes d’ISOTRETINOINE ACNETRAIT 20 mg, capsule molle.
paternal.source_label: ANSM, RCP ISOTRETINOINE ACNETRAIT 20 mg, capsule molle, section 4.4 (Hommes), RCP updated 30/07/2026

other_effects.text: The US label reports cases of IQ below 85, with or without other abnormalities, in children exposed before birth, and an increased risk of miscarriage and premature birth.
other_effects.quote: Cases of IQ scores less than 85 with or without other abnormalities have been reported in children exposed in utero to isotretinoin. An increased risk of spontaneous abortion and premature births have been reported with isotretinoin exposure during pregnancy.
other_effects.source_label: US FDA label, ABSORICA / ABSORICA LD (Sun Pharmaceutical), section 8.1 Human Data, via openFDA (SPL version 21)

regulatory.text: The French label contraindicates isotretinoin in pregnancy and breastfeeding, and in women who could become pregnant unless every condition of the Pregnancy Prevention Programme is met.
regulatory.quote: L'isotrétinoïne est contre-indiquée chez les femmes enceintes ou qui allaitent (voir rubrique 4.6). L'isotrétinoïne est contre-indiquée chez les femmes en âge de procréer sauf si toutes les conditions du « Programme de Prévention de la Grossesse » sont remplies
regulatory.source_label: ANSM, RCP ISOTRETINOINE ACNETRAIT 20 mg, capsule molle, section 4.3 Contre-indications, RCP updated 30/07/2026

monitoring.text: If pregnancy occurs, the US label says to stop isotretinoin immediately and refer to an obstetrician-gynaecologist experienced in reproductive toxicity, and that no accurate means can determine prenatally whether an exposed fetus is affected.
monitoring.quote: There are no accurate means of determining prenatally whether an exposed fetus has been affected. If pregnancy occurs, discontinue ABSORICA/ABSORICA LD immediately and refer the patient to an Obstetrician- Gynecologist experienced in reproductive toxicity for further evaluation and counseling
monitoring.source_label: US FDA label, ABSORICA / ABSORICA LD (Sun Pharmaceutical), boxed warning, via openFDA (SPL version 21)

evidence_base.text: A 2021 systematic review and meta-analysis of 10 studies with 2,783 isotretinoin-exposed women found a 15% sample-weighted major-malformation rate, and only 3 studies had an unexposed comparison group.
evidence_base.quote: Ten eligible studies that combined 2,783 isotretinoin-exposed women were included in our study. The rate of MM weighted for the sample size was 15%. Three studies that included an unexposed comparison group were eligible for the meta-analysis.
evidence_base.source_label: Choi et al., The rates of major malformations after gestational exposure to isotretinoin: a systematic review and meta-analysis, Obstet Gynecol Sci 2021;64(4):364-373 (abstract)

window.text: ANSM counts from treatment: a pregnancy that starts during acitretin treatment or within 3 years after stopping carries a very high risk of major malformations in the fetus.
window.quote: La survenue, en dépit des mesures contraceptives, d'une grossesse au cours d'un traitement par acitrétine ou dans les 3 ans qui suivent son arrêt, comporte un risque très élevé de malformations majeures chez le fœtus.
window.source_label: ANSM, SORIATANE 25 mg gélule, RCP section 4.6 (Base de données publique des médicaments)

dose.text: The US label states that the blood-level threshold for increased birth defects has not been established for acitretin in humans, and post-treatment contraception time cannot be calculated precisely.
dose.quote: Because this threshold has not been established for acitretin in humans and because elimination rates vary among patients, the duration of posttherapy contraception to achieve adequate elimination cannot be calculated precisely.
dose.source_label: US FDA label, Acitretin capsules (Sigmapharm), boxed CONTRAINDICATIONS AND WARNINGS, via openFDA

effects.text: The US label lists reported major fetal abnormalities with acitretin or etretinate, including meningomyelocele, meningoencephalocele, multiple synostoses, facial dysmorphia, and limb or digit defects (syndactyly, absent terminal phalanges, hip, ankle and forearm malformations).
effects.quote: Major human fetal abnormalities associated with acitretin and/or etretinate administration have been reported including meningomyelocele; meningoencephalocele; multiple synostoses; facial dysmorphia; syndactyly; absence of terminal phalanges; malformations of hip, ankle, and forearm
effects.source_label: US FDA label, Acitretin capsules (Sigmapharm), boxed CONTRAINDICATIONS AND WARNINGS, via openFDA

before_after.text: ANSM requires women who can become pregnant to use contraception from at least 1 month before acitretin, throughout treatment and for at least 3 years after stopping, even without periods.
before_after.quote: Une méthode de contraception doit être utilisée pendant au moins 1 mois avant le début du traitement, pendant toute la durée du traitement et pendant au moins 3 ans après l'arrêt du traitement par acitrétine, même en cas d’aménorrhée.
before_after.source_label: ANSM, SORIATANE 25 mg gélule (acitrétine), RCP section 4.4, Contraception (Base de données publique des médicaments)

paternal.text: The US label says acitretin in semen appears to pose little, if any, risk to a fetus during or after a man's treatment, but the no-effect limit for teratogenicity is unknown.
paternal.quote: although it appears that residual acitretin in seminal fluid poses little, if any, risk to a fetus while a male patient is taking the drug or after it is discontinued, the no-effect limit for teratogenicity is unknown
paternal.source_label: US FDA label, Acitretin capsules (Sigmapharm), boxed CONTRAINDICATIONS AND WARNINGS, Important Information for Males, via openFDA

other_effects.text: Beyond malformations, acitretin's French product information states that there is also an increased risk of miscarriage.
other_effects.quote: Il existe également une augmentation du risque d'avortement spontané.
other_effects.source_label: ANSM, SORIATANE 25 mg gélule (acitrétine), RCP section 4.6 Grossesse (Base de données publique des médicaments)

regulatory.text: France's product information strictly contraindicates acitretin in pregnant women and in women who can become pregnant unless every condition of the pregnancy prevention programme is met.
regulatory.quote: SORIATANE 25 mg, gélule est strictement contre-indiqué chez : - les femmes enceintes, - les femmes en âge de procréer, sauf si toutes les conditions du « Programme de prévention de la grossesse » sont remplies.
regulatory.source_label: ANSM, SORIATANE 25 mg gélule (acitrétine), RCP section 4.4, Effets tératogènes (Base de données publique des médicaments)

monitoring.text: If a woman becomes pregnant on acitretin, ANSM requires stopping treatment and referring her to a physician specialised or experienced in teratology for evaluation and advice.
monitoring.quote: En cas de grossesse chez une femme traitée par acitrétine, le traitement doit être interrompu et la patiente doit être orientée vers un médecin spécialisé ou expérimenté en tératologie pour évaluation et conseil.
monitoring.source_label: ANSM, SORIATANE 25 mg gélule (acitrétine), RCP section 4.4, Programme de prévention de la grossesse (Base de données publique des médicaments)

evidence_base.text: Manufacturers' pharmacovigilance data assessed by EU regulators in 2018 counted 442 acitretin pregnancy cases since marketing, 132 conceived during treatment and 260 after it.
evidence_base.quote: Acitretin: 442 pregnancy cases (132 related to conception during treatment, 260 after completing treatment);
evidence_base.source_label: EMA PRAC assessment report, Article 31 referral on retinoid-containing medicinal products, section 2.4.1 Teratogenic effects, oral retinoids

window.text: ANSM counts from treatment: pregnancy during alitretinoin (Toctino) treatment or within the month after stopping carries a very high risk of very severe malformations.
window.quote: La survenue, en dépit des mesures contraceptives, d'une grossesse au cours d'un traitement par TOCTINO ou dans le mois qui suit son arrêt, comporte un risque très élevé de malformations très sévères et graves chez le fœtus.
window.source_label: ANSM, TOCTINO 30 mg capsule molle, RCP section 4.6 (Base de données publique des médicaments)

effects.text: EMA's harmonised leaflet text says oral alitretinoin can cause serious abnormalities of the baby's brain, face, ear, eye, heart, thymus and parathyroid glands, and makes miscarriage more likely.
effects.quote: it can cause serious abnormalities of the unborn baby’s brain, face, ear, eye, heart and certain glands (thymus gland and parathyroid gland). It also makes a miscarriage more likely.
effects.source_label: EMA, Retinoid Article 31 referral 2018, Annex III (package leaflet text for oral acitretin, alitretinoin and isotretinoin)

before_after.text: ANSM requires women who can become pregnant to use contraception from at least 1 month before alitretinoin, throughout treatment and for at least 1 month after stopping, even without periods.
before_after.quote: Une méthode de contraception doit être utilisée pendant au moins 1 mois avant le début du traitement, pendant toute la durée du traitement et pendant au moins 1 mois après l'arrêt du traitement par alitrétinoïne, même en cas d'aménorrhée.
before_after.source_label: ANSM, TOCTINO 30 mg capsule molle (alitrétinoïne), RCP section 4.4, Contraception (Base de données publique des médicaments)

paternal.text: ANSM says available data suggest that a woman's exposure through the semen of men taking alitretinoin is not high enough to be linked to its teratogenic effects.
paternal.quote: Les données disponibles suggèrent que le niveau d’exposition maternelle à partir du sperme de patients traités par TOCTINO n’est pas suffisant pour être associé aux effets tératogènes de TOCTINO.
paternal.source_label: ANSM, TOCTINO 30 mg capsule molle (alitrétinoïne), RCP section 4.4, Hommes (Base de données publique des médicaments)

other_effects.text: Canada's product monograph states that pregnancy during alitretinoin treatment or within one month after stopping carries a risk of malformation and an increased risk of spontaneous abortion.
other_effects.quote: Pregnancy occurring during treatment with HANZEMA and for one month after its discontinuation, carries the risk of fetal malformation and the increased risk of spontaneous abortion
other_effects.source_label: Health Canada product monograph, HANZEMA (alitretinoin capsules, Dr. Reddy's), Warnings and Precautions, Pregnancy

regulatory.text: France's product information strictly contraindicates alitretinoin in pregnant women and in women who can become pregnant unless every condition of the pregnancy prevention programme is met.
regulatory.quote: TOCTINO est strictement contre-indiqué chez : · les femmes enceintes · les femmes en âge de procréer, sauf si toutes les conditions du Programme de prévention de la grossesse sont remplies
regulatory.source_label: ANSM, TOCTINO 30 mg capsule molle (alitrétinoïne), RCP section 4.4, Effets tératogènes (Base de données publique des médicaments)

monitoring.text: If a woman becomes pregnant on alitretinoin, ANSM requires stopping treatment and referring her to a physician specialised or experienced in teratology for evaluation and advice.
monitoring.quote: En cas de grossesse chez une femme traitée par l’alitrétinoïne, le traitement doit être interrompu et la patiente doit être orientée vers un médecin spécialisé ou expérimenté en tératologie pour évaluation et conseil.
monitoring.source_label: ANSM, TOCTINO 30 mg capsule molle (alitrétinoïne), RCP section 4.4, Programme de prévention de la grossesse (Base de données publique des médicaments)

evidence_base.text: Manufacturers' pharmacovigilance data assessed by EU regulators in 2018 counted 17 oral alitretinoin pregnancy cases since marketing, 12 conceived during treatment and 4 more than one month after stopping treatment.
evidence_base.quote: Alitretinoin: 17 pregnancy cases (12 related to conception during treatment, 4 more than one month after stopping treatment);
evidence_base.source_label: EMA PRAC assessment report, Article 31 referral on retinoid-containing medicinal products, section 2.4.1 Teratogenic effects, oral retinoids

window.text: The US label reports malformations in rats given bexarotene by mouth on gestation days 7 to 17, and it states no human risk window.
window.quote: Bexarotene caused malformations when administered orally to pregnant rats during days 7-17 of gestation.
window.source_label: US FDA label, TARGRETIN (bexarotene) capsules, Bausch Health, section 8.1 Pregnancy, Animal Data (openFDA)

dose.text: EMA states that a safety margin for human teratogenicity has not been demonstrated for bexarotene, based on its comparison of animal and patient exposures.
dose.quote: Based on the comparison of animal and patient exposures to bexarotene, a margin of safety for human teratogenicity has not been demonstrated
dose.source_label: EMA, Targretin EPAR product information, SmPC section 4.6

effects.text: For oral retinoids as a group, ENTIS lists multiple malformations, including central nervous system, orofacial cleft, cardiovascular, skeletal, limb and ear defects, as well as facial dysmorphia.
effects.quote: Multiple malformations including central nervous system abnormalities, orofacial clefts, cardiovascular, skeletal, limb and ear. Facial dysmorphia.
effects.source_label: Bluett-Duncan et al., Birth Defects Res 2025;117(9):e2497, Table 1 (ENTIS / ConcePTION); the effects cell spans all five oral retinoids

absolute_risk.text: EMA's 2018 review reports retinoid embryopathy in up to 30% of fetuses exposed to oral retinoids as a class, and it gives no rate specific to bexarotene.
absolute_risk.quote: The human data on congenital malformations after oral retinoid exposure show a significant risk of retinoid embryopathy (of up to 30% of fetuses exposed)
absolute_risk.source_label: EMA, retinoid Article 31 referral (EMEA/H/A-31/1446), Annex II scientific conclusions (EC decision 21 June 2018; Annex II first published 2 July 2018)

before_after.text: The US label requires effective contraception from 1 month before starting bexarotene, throughout treatment and for at least 1 month after stopping it.
before_after.quote: Effective contraception must be used for 1 month prior to the initiation of therapy, during therapy and for at least 1 month following discontinuation of therapy
before_after.source_label: US FDA label, TARGRETIN (bexarotene) capsules, Bausch Health, section 8.3 Females and Males of Reproductive Potential, via openFDA (DailyMed SPL version 16)

paternal.text: The EU product information says men taking bexarotene whose partners are, may be or could become pregnant must use condoms during intercourse throughout treatment and for at least one month after the last dose.
paternal.quote: Male patients with sexual partners who are pregnant, possibly pregnant, or may potentially become pregnant must use condoms during sexual intercourse while taking bexarotene and for at least one month after the last dose.
paternal.source_label: EMA, Targretin EPAR product information, SmPC section 4.6 Contraception in males and females

other_effects.text: In animal studies only, bexarotene given by mouth to pregnant rats at more than 10 mg/kg/day caused developmental mortality.
other_effects.quote: At doses greater than 10 mg/kg/day, bexarotene caused developmental mortality.
other_effects.source_label: US FDA label, TARGRETIN (bexarotene) capsules, Bausch Health, section 8.1 Pregnancy, Animal Data, via openFDA (DailyMed SPL version 16)

regulatory.text: The EU product information contraindicates bexarotene in pregnancy and breastfeeding, and in women of child-bearing potential who do not use effective contraception.
regulatory.quote: Pregnancy and lactation. Women of child-bearing potential without effective birth-control measures.
regulatory.source_label: EMA, Targretin EPAR product information, SmPC section 4.3 Contraindications

monitoring.text: If pregnancy occurs during treatment, the US label says to stop bexarotene immediately and to advise the woman of the potential risk to the fetus.
monitoring.quote: If pregnancy does occur during treatment with TARGRETIN, immediately discontinue the drug and advise the pregnant female of the potential risk to a fetus.
monitoring.source_label: US FDA label, TARGRETIN (bexarotene) capsules, Bausch Health, section 8.1 Pregnancy, Risk Summary, via openFDA (DailyMed SPL version 16)

evidence_base.text: EMA's product information for the oral capsules says there are no adequate data on bexarotene use in pregnant women and that animal studies have shown reproductive toxicity.
evidence_base.quote: There are no adequate data from the use of bexarotene in pregnant women. Studies in animals have shown reproductive toxicity.
evidence_base.source_label: EMA, Targretin (oral capsules) EPAR product information, SmPC section 4.6 Pregnancy

window.text: France's product information says human data on tretinoin in pregnancy are limited, but there is a high risk of severe fetal malformations, particularly when it is given in the first trimester.
window.quote: les données sur l'utilisation de la trétinoïne chez la femme enceinte sont limitées mais il existe un risque élevé de malformations sévères du fœtus, en particulier lorsque la trétinoïne est administrée au cours du premier trimestre de la grossesse
window.source_label: ANSM, VESANOID 10 mg capsule molle, RCP section 4.6 Grossesse (Base de données publique des médicaments), RCP updated 22/04/2025

dose.text: In animal studies, the US label reports external, soft tissue and skeletal alterations above 0.7, 2 and 7 mg/kg/day in mice, rats and hamsters respectively, and at 10 mg/kg/day in monkeys.
dose.quote: Gross external, soft tissue and skeletal alterations occurred at doses higher than 0.7 mg/kg/day in mice, 2 mg/kg/day in rats, 7 mg/kg/day in hamsters, and at a dose of 10 mg/kg/day, the only dose tested, in pigtail monkeys
dose.source_label: US FDA label, tretinoin capsules (Par Health USA), section 8.1 Pregnancy, Animal Data (openFDA)

effects.text: From human exposure to retinoids, the US label reports malformations of the central nervous system, musculoskeletal system, external ear, eye, thymus and great vessels, plus facial dysmorphia, cleft palate and parathyroid hormone deficiency.
effects.quote: Reported malformations include abnormalities of the central nervous system, musculoskeletal system, external ear, eye, thymus and great vessels; and facial dysmorphia, cleft palate, and parathyroid hormone deficiency.
effects.source_label: US FDA label, tretinoin capsules (Par Health USA), section 8.1 Human Data (openFDA)

absolute_risk.text: EMA's 2018 review reports retinoid embryopathy in up to 30% of fetuses exposed to oral retinoids as a class, and it gives no rate specific to tretinoin.
absolute_risk.quote: The human data on congenital malformations after oral retinoid exposure show a significant risk of retinoid embryopathy (of up to 30% of fetuses exposed)
absolute_risk.source_label: EMA, retinoid Article 31 referral (EMEA/H/A-31/1446), Annex II scientific conclusions (EC decision 21 June 2018; Annex II first published 2 July 2018)

before_after.text: For women who could become pregnant, the US label requires a negative pregnancy test before starting and says to advise two effective contraceptive methods during treatment and for 1 month after the last dose.
before_after.quote: Females of reproductive potential must have a negative pregnancy test before initiating tretinoin capsules. Advise females of reproductive potential to use two effective methods of contraception during treatment with tretinoin capsules and for 1 month after the last dose.
before_after.source_label: US FDA label, tretinoin capsules (Par Health USA), boxed warning, via openFDA (DailyMed SPL version 20)

paternal.text: The US label says men taking oral tretinoin whose female partners could become pregnant should be advised to use effective contraception during treatment and for 1 week after the last dose.
paternal.quote: Advise males with female partners of reproductive potential to use effective contraception during and after treatment with tretinoin capsules and for 1 week after the last dose.
paternal.source_label: US FDA label, tretinoin capsules (Par Health USA), section 8.3 Use in Females and Males of Reproductive Potential, via openFDA (DailyMed SPL version 20)

other_effects.text: The US label says exposure to retinoids, the class tretinoin belongs to, in human pregnancy increases the risk of spontaneous abortion and premature birth as well as major malformations.
other_effects.quote: Tretinoin capsules are a retinoid and there is an increased risk of major congenital malformations, spontaneous abortions and premature births following exposure to retinoids during pregnancy in humans.
other_effects.source_label: US FDA label, tretinoin capsules (Par Health USA), section 8.1 Pregnancy, Risk Summary, via openFDA (DailyMed SPL version 20)

regulatory.text: Health Canada's product monograph places tretinoin's teratogenicity in its serious-warnings box and contraindicates its use in pregnant women.
regulatory.quote: Teratogenic effect: Tretinoin is highly teratogenic. Its use is contraindicated in pregnant women.
regulatory.source_label: Health Canada, VESANOID (tretinoin) 10 mg capsules product monograph (Cheplapharm), section 3 Serious Warnings and Precautions Box

monitoring.text: If Vesanoid is given in early pregnancy, the French product information says the patient must be told of the risk of teratogenic effects and of severe fetal malformations.
monitoring.quote: Si Vesanoid est administré en début de grossesse, la patiente doit être avertie du risque d'effets tératogènes de Vesanoid et du risque de malformations fœtales sévères.
monitoring.source_label: ANSM, VESANOID 10 mg capsule molle, RCP section 4.6 Grossesse (Base de données publique des médicaments)

evidence_base.text: A 2020 systematic review of 66 articles, 53 of them single case reports, found 92 pregnant women with APL eligible for induction, about three-quarters treated with all-trans retinoic acid alone or with chemotherapy.
evidence_base.quote: Sixty-six articles met the eligibility criteria (53 single case reports). Ninety-two patients were eligible for induction therapy, with most them being treated with all-trans retinoic acid alone (32%) or combined with chemotherapy (43%)
evidence_base.source_label: Santolaria A, Perales A, Montesinos P, Sanz MA. Acute promyelocytic leukemia during pregnancy: a systematic review of the literature. Cancers (Basel) 2020;12(4):968, abstract
